transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um… I’m here because I’ve been getting really stuck on how my face looks, mostly around my jaw and neck. It probably sounds silly, and people tell me it looks normal, but I keep seeing this sagging, uneven area there.

I just feel like when families or nurses at work, or people at church, look at me, that’s the first thing they notice. I know that may not make sense, but I can’t seem to stop thinking about it.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain social situations, like going out in public or interacting with others, because of how your jaw and neck look?

A little, yes… I mean, I still go to work and everything, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But I have turned down chances to help lead meetings or do more of the supervisory parts because I get worried people will be looking at my face and neck instead of listening to me.

And, um… sometimes getting ready takes so long that I fall behind on paperwork, because I’m trying to make myself look presentable enough. I’ve also skipped some book club and walking club things lately, not because I don’t want to go, but because getting ready just feels like too much. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself doing things like checking mirrors often, touching or measuring the area, or trying to cover it up with makeup, clothing, or hairstyles? If so, how often does that happen?

I do, yes… maybe more than I should. I don’t want to sound vain, because it’s not really like that, but before I leave for work or if I have a meeting, I keep going back to the bathroom mirror and adjusting my collar or my hair around my neck.

Then I’ll think, “Okay, it’s fine,” but a few minutes later I’ll check my phone camera just to make sure it doesn’t look strange. Sometimes I’ll ask my daughter, too, like, “Does this look weird?” I know that probably gets annoying for her.

It’s not all day nonstop, but it happens enough that I’ve been late more than once because I can’t seem to just leave it alone.
Has this concern about your jaw and neck ever caused you significant emotional distress, like feelings of shame, sadness, or anxiety, that interfere with your day-to-day life?

Yes… I think it has, though I don’t want to make it sound overly dramatic. It’s embarrassing to admit.

I’ve passed up chances to help lead meetings or take on more of the supervisory parts at work because I worry people will be staring at my face and neck instead of listening to me. And sometimes I get so stuck trying to make myself look presentable that I end up behind on paperwork.

I’ve also stopped going to some of my book club and walking club things, not because I don’t like them, but because getting ready just feels like too much. So… yes, I guess it does interfere more than I’d like to admit.
